guide.summary: A big, slow grazer that eats algae and fungus threads and can rest when food or water runs out.
guide.biology: Real water bears are tiny eight-legged animals that graze on algae and can curl up and rest when their home dries out.
guide.rules: Lives in water, gel or sediment with moisture of at least 0.2. Moves 0.35 cells per second and notices food up to 3 cells away. Catches algae (Sunbead, Glasswheel, Shadeleaf, Turnleaf, Raftball) or one fungus segment at a time (Threadlace, Cordweaver, Sporeveil) on contact, stores a meal of up to twice its own body, and waits 5 seconds before the next catch. After 20 seconds without food, or 10 seconds where it is far too dry, it can rest if it has at least 15 energy: it spends 10 energy to prepare, then uses only 0.01 energy per second. It wakes after food and moisture have been back for 10 seconds, spending 5 energy.
guide.example: Turn on drying in a dish with Waterbears and Sunbeads, then wet the ground again later and watch the resting Waterbears wake up.
